\section{Threshold Functions --- Affine Khintchine}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.AffineKhintchine
\subsection*{Threshold Functions --- Affine Khintchine: Introduction}
Coordinate influences and antipodal symmetry give a sharp affine comparison between the first absolute moment and the coefficient second moment.

\subsection*{Threshold Functions --- Affine Khintchine: Results}

\begin{lemma}[Absolute values decrease coordinate influence]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.influence_abs_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.expect_mono, BooleanAnalysis.flipBit, BooleanAnalysis.influence}
\difficulty{3}
For every dimension $n\ge0$, real-valued function $h$ on $\{0,1\}^n$, and coordinate
$i\in[n]$, the influence of $i$ on the pointwise absolute value $|h|$ is at most its
influence on $h$: $\mathrm{Inf}_i[|h|]\le \mathrm{Inf}_i[h]$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Variance and influence inequality]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.spectral_inequality}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff_empty, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.parseval, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence_eq_sum_sq_deg, BooleanAnalysis.weightLevel}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and let $g:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$. With expectation taken uniformly
on the cube, let $\mathrm{Inf}(g)$ be the sum of its coordinate influences and let
$W_1(g)=\sum_{|S|=1}\widehat g(S)^2$ be its Fourier weight at level one. Then
$2\bigl(\mathbb E[g^2]-(\mathbb E g)^2\bigr)\le \mathrm{Inf}(g)+W_1(g)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[First-level weight from antipodal differences]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.weightLevel1_antipode_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.expect_add, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.expect_const, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.expect_const_mul, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.expect_mono, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.flipSet_univ, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.fourierCoeff_comp_flipSet, BooleanAnalysis.chiS, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.parseval, BooleanAnalysis.weightLevel}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $g:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $a\in\mathbb
R$. If $|g(x)-g(\bar x)|\le 2|a|$ for every $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, where $\bar x$ is obtained
by flipping every bit of $x$, then the Fourier weight of $g$ at level $1$ is at most
$a^2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Antipodal sum of an affine Walsh polynomial]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.affine_sum_antipode}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.HasDegreeAtMost, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.eval, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.eval_of_degree_le_one, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign_not}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n\ge 0$, and let $p$ be a real coefficient family on the subsets of
$\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ whose coefficients vanish on every subset of size greater than $1$.
For every Boolean vector $x$, the values of its Walsh polynomial at $x$ and at the
coordinatewise complement of $x$ sum to twice the constant coefficient: $P_p(x)+P_p(\bar
x)=2p(\varnothing)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Influence identity for degree-one polynomials]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.affine_influence}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.HasDegreeAtMost, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.eval, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence_eq_sum_sq_deg}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and let $p$ be a real coefficient family indexed by subsets of
$\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, with $p(S)=0$ whenever $|S|>1$. Evaluate $p$ in the Walsh basis on
the Boolean cube, and let $I[P]$ denote the sum over coordinates of the uniform
expectations of one quarter of the squared change in $P$ under a bit flip. Then
$I[P]+p(\varnothing)^2=\sum_{S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}p(S)^2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[First and second moments for affine polynomials]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.affine_khintchine_sq}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.HasDegreeAtMost, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.eval, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.innerProduct_eval_self, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.affine_influence, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.affine_sum_antipode, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.influence_abs_le, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.spectral_inequality, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.weightLevel1_antipode_le, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence, BooleanAnalysis.weightLevel}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and let $p$ be a real coefficient family indexed by subsets of
$\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, with $p(S)=0$ whenever $|S|>1$. If $P$ is the Walsh polynomial
$P(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}p(S)\chi_S(x)$, then
$\sum_{S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}p(S)^2\le 2\bigl(\mathbb
E_{x\sim\mathrm{Unif}(\{-1,1\}^n)}|P(x)|\bigr)^2$.
\end{theorem}
